india.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 6-digit numeric code. The first digit represents the region, the second the sub-region, the third the sorting district, and the last three indicate the specific post office.

states.name: Karnataka
states.description: Known as the tech capital of India, Karnataka features a mix of historical monuments, palaces, and a booming software industry.

states.name: Maharashtra
states.description: Home to Mumbai, the financial capital of India, and famous ancient rock-cut temples like Ajanta and Ellora.

states.name: Delhi
states.description: The national capital territory of India, containing historic landmarks like the Red Fort, Qutub Minar, and India Gate.

states.name: Tamil Nadu
states.description: Famous for its Dravidian-style Hindu temples, classical music, and rich history dating back to ancient Tamil dynasties.

states.name: West Bengal
states.description: A cultural hub in eastern India, famed for its literature, architectural relics of the British Raj, and the Sundarbans mangrove forest.

india.generalPostalTrivia: The Postal Index Number (PIN) system was introduced on August 15, 1972, to simplify mail routing and eliminate confusion caused by similar place names and diverse languages.

united states.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 5-digit number indicating the national area, sectional center facility, and local post office. Often appended with 4 digits (ZIP+4) for more precise sorting.

states.name: California
states.description: America's most populous state, home to Hollywood, Silicon Valley, wine country, and diverse national parks like Yosemite.

states.name: New York
states.description: Renowned for New York City, Wall Street, Broadway, and upstate treasures like Niagara Falls and the Adirondacks.

states.name: Texas
states.description: The Lone Star State, characterized by its vast deserts, major energy companies, historic sites like the Alamo, and NASA space center.

states.name: Florida
states.description: The Sunshine State, featuring hundreds of miles of beaches, major theme parks in Orlando, and the unique Everglades ecosystem.

states.name: Washington
states.description: Located in the Pacific Northwest, Washington is famous for its evergreen forests, Mount Rainier, and tech giants based in Seattle.

united states.generalPostalTrivia: ZIP stands for Zone Improvement Plan. It was introduced in 1963 by the United States Post Office Department to automate mail sorting as mail volume grew rapidly.

canada.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A six-character alphanumeric code where letters and numbers alternate. The first character represents a specific postal province or district.

states.name: Ontario
states.description: Canada's economic engine, featuring Toronto's CN Tower, the federal capital Ottawa, and the spectacular Niagara Falls.

states.name: Quebec
states.description: A predominantly French-speaking province, famous for its historic Old Quebec City, maple syrup production, and Montreal's vibrant culture.

states.name: British Columbia
states.description: Canada's westernmost province, known for its majestic Pacific coastline, Whistler ski resorts, and the metropolitan city of Vancouver.

states.name: Alberta
states.description: Famous for the Rocky Mountains, Banff and Jasper National Parks, and vast oil and gas reserves.

canada.generalPostalTrivia: Canada Post uses a specialized sorting code for Santa Claus: 'H0H 0H0', North Pole, Canada. Every year, millions of children write letters to this postal code and receive replies.

australia.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 4-digit numeric code. The first digit represents the state or territory, followed by sub-divisions.

states.name: New South Wales
states.description: Features the landmark Opera House and Harbour Bridge in Sydney, beautiful beaches, and the Blue Mountains.

states.name: Victoria
states.description: A cultural and sporting capital centered in Melbourne, known for its Victorian architecture, arts scenes, and coffee culture.

states.name: Queensland
states.description: Home to the tropical Great Barrier Reef, pristine sandy beaches of the Gold Coast, and lush rainforests.

states.name: Western Australia
states.description: Australia's largest state, renowned for its remote outback, Margaret River wine region, and the sunny capital city Perth.

australia.generalPostalTrivia: Australia Post was founded shortly after federation in 1901. It operates one of the world's most sparsely populated delivery networks, stretching across the entire continent.

united kingdom.postalCodeRegexExplanation: An alphanumeric code between 5 and 7 characters split by a space. The outward code identifies the district, while the inward code identifies the street or unit.

states.name: England
states.description: Features historic universities like Oxford and Cambridge, industrial heritage in Manchester, and the capital metropolis London.

states.name: Scotland
states.description: Famous for its Highlands, historic castles, Edinburgh festival, deep lochs, and cultural heritage.

states.name: Wales
states.description: A mountainous country known for its Celtic culture, rugged coastlines, and a vast density of historic castles per square mile.

states.name: Northern Ireland
states.description: Known for the dramatic basalt columns of the Giant's Causeway, historic Belfast shipyards, and beautiful green valleys.

united kingdom.generalPostalTrivia: The modern postal system was revolutionized in the UK in 1840 with the introduction of the Penny Black, the world's first adhesive postage stamp, making postage cheap and uniform.

germany.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 5-digit numeric code introduced in 1993 after reunification. The first digit represents the zone, and the second digit denotes the region.

states.name: Bavaria
states.description: Germany's southern state, famous for Neuschwanstein Castle, Munich's Oktoberfest, and the Alpine mountain range.

states.name: Berlin
states.description: A city-state and the capital of Germany, known for its history, underground music, art, and landmark Brandenburg Gate.

states.name: Hamburg
states.description: A major port city-state in northern Germany, connected to the North Sea, famous for its canals, port district, and Elbphilharmonie concert hall.

states.name: North Rhine-Westphalia
states.description: Germany's most populous state, containing the industrial Ruhr area and historic cities like Cologne and Düsseldorf.

germany.generalPostalTrivia: Germany was the first country to introduce a postal code system (Postleitzahl) in 1941, during World War II, which was later completely restructured in 1961 (West) and 1965 (East).

japan.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 7-digit numeric code formatted as 3 digits followed by a hyphen and then 4 digits. The first three digits indicate the regional route, and the last four represent the specific delivery zone.

states.name: Tokyo
states.description: The ultra-modern metropolis and capital of Japan, combining neon skyscrapers, historic shrines, and busy districts like Shibuya.

states.name: Osaka
states.description: A large port city and commercial center, famous for its street food, nightlife, and historic Osaka Castle.

states.name: Kyoto
states.description: Japan's ancient imperial capital, famous for thousands of classical Buddhist temples, gardens, imperial palaces, and geisha traditions.

states.name: Hokkaido
states.description: Japan's northernmost island, known for its volcanoes, hot springs (onsen), ski resorts, and the annual Sapporo Snow Festival.

japan.generalPostalTrivia: Japan Post was privatized in 2007. It runs one of the world's most integrated networks, combining postal delivery, savings accounts, and life insurance services.

brazil.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 5-digit number followed by a hyphen and 3 digits. The digits represent regions, sub-regions, sectors, sub-sectors, and delivery divisions.

states.name: São Paulo
states.description: Brazil's economic powerhouse state, centered around the massive metropolis of São Paulo, famous for coffee production and cultural diversity.

states.name: Rio de Janeiro
states.description: Famous worldwide for Copacabana and Ipanema beaches, the Christ the Redeemer statue, and its energetic Carnival festival.

states.name: Minas Gerais
states.description: A historic state known for colonial-era gold-mining towns, dramatic hills, and rich cuisine including traditional cheese (pão de queijo).

brazil.generalPostalTrivia: The CEP (Código de Endereçamento Postal) system was created in 1971 by Correios (the state-owned postal service of Brazil) to handle the country's rapid urban growth.

france.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 5-digit code. The first two digits represent the department number, and the last three identify the local post office or distribution center.

states.name: Île-de-France
states.description: The historic region surrounding Paris, featuring the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre Museum, and the Palace of Versailles.

states.name: Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
states.description: Renowned for its sunny French Riviera, lavender fields of Provence, and historic cities like Nice, Cannes, and Avignon.

states.name: Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes
states.description: Home to the French Alps, including Mont Blanc, beautiful lakes, and the culinary capital city of Lyon.

france.generalPostalTrivia: French postal codes use a system called Cedex (Courrier d'Entreprise à Distribution Exceptionnelle) for large volume business recipients, sorting their mail directly to their own dedicated postal codes.

south africa.language: 11 Official Languages (including Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans, English)
south africa.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 4-digit code. The first two digits indicate the routing district and province, and the last two represent the specific post office or box.

states.name: Gauteng
states.description: The smallest but most populous province, featuring the economic powerhouse Johannesburg and the administrative capital Pretoria.

states.name: Western Cape
states.description: Famous for the flat-topped Table Mountain, spectacular coastal drives, wine estates, and the legislative capital Cape Town.

states.name: KwaZulu-Natal
states.description: Known for its warm beaches, Drakensberg mountains, historic battlefields, and Zulu cultural heritage.

south africa.generalPostalTrivia: South African postal codes distinguish between street delivery addresses (odd codes or low ranges) and post office box delivery addresses (even codes or higher ranges) to optimize sorting.

russia.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 6-digit numeric code. The first three digits indicate the regional postal hub, and the last three indicate the local post office.

states.name: Moscow
states.description: Russia's capital city-state, featuring the Kremlin, Red Square, Saint Basil's Cathedral, and a massive subway system.

states.name: Saint Petersburg
states.description: The cultural capital of Russia, famous for its canals, Hermitage Museum, and historic architecture built by Peter the Great.

states.name: Novosibirsk Oblast
states.description: Located in Siberia, hosting Novosibirsk, the third-most populous city in Russia, and the science town Akademgorodok.

russia.generalPostalTrivia: Russian postal codes are known as the Russian Postal Index. They were standard six-digit identifiers designed to span across the massive 11 time zones of the country.

china.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 6-digit numeric code. The first two digits represent the province/municipality, the third indicates the postal zone, the fourth is the county/city, and the last two denote the specific post office.

states.name: Guangdong
states.description: A southern coastal province and global manufacturing hub, containing the major economic cities of Guangzhou and Shenzhen.

states.name: Beijing
states.description: China's capital, containing historic sites like the Forbidden City, Tiananmen Square, and nearby sections of the Great Wall.

states.name: Shanghai
states.description: A global financial center and major port city, famous for the futuristic skyline of Lujiazui and colonial-era Bund promenade.

states.name: Sichuan
states.description: Located in southwest China, famous for its spicy cuisine, giant panda reserves, and dramatic mountain landscapes.

china.generalPostalTrivia: China Post operates one of the largest postal systems in the world. It was established in 1949 and also serves rural remote villages through specialized postal service routes.

italy.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 5-digit code. The first two digits indicate the province, and the last three indicate the specific town or city district.

states.name: Lazio
states.description: Home to Italy's capital city Rome and the Vatican City, with ancient Roman ruins like the Colosseum.

states.name: Lombardy
states.description: Italy's economic center in the north, home to the global fashion capital Milan and scenic Alpine lakes like Lake Como.

states.name: Tuscany
states.description: Famous for its rolling vineyards, Chianti wines, art history in Florence, and the Leaning Tower of Pisa.

italy.generalPostalTrivia: CAP stands for Codice di Avviamento Postale. It was introduced in 1967 to speed up mail deliveries across Italy's complex regional postal systems.

spain.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 5-digit number where the first two digits represent the province code (matching the alphabetical order of Spanish provinces), and the last three denote the city or postal zone.

states.name: Madrid
states.description: The central region hosting Spain's capital, containing the Royal Palace, Prado Museum, and lively town plazas.

states.name: Catalonia
states.description: Located in northeast Spain, famous for Barcelona's Sagrada Família, Gaudí architecture, and Costa Brava beaches.

states.name: Andalusia
states.description: Southern Spain, known for Moorish architecture like the Alhambra in Granada, Seville Cathedral, and flamenco music.

spain.generalPostalTrivia: Spain's Correos system utilizes a fully automated sorting infrastructure. The first two digits of the postal code match the official province codes (01-52).

mexico.postalCodeRegexExplanation: A 5-digit code. The first two digits indicate the state or administrative zone, and the remaining digits represent the municipality and neighborhood.

states.name: Ciudad de México
states.description: The massive capital city-state, containing historic ruins of Tenochtitlan, colonial cathedrals, and rich culinary scenes.

states.name: Jalisco
states.description: Known as the birthplace of tequila, mariachi music, and rich cultural traditions, situated in western Mexico.

states.name: Nuevo León
states.description: A major northern industrial state, home to the business and technological hub city of Monterrey, surrounded by the Sierra Madre mountains.

mexico.generalPostalTrivia: Mexico's postal codes are managed by Correos de México. The codes are allocated counter-clockwise geographically, starting from central Mexico City outwards.

560001.description: Located in the heart of Bengaluru (formerly Bangalore) near Cubbon Park and Vidhana Soudha. It represents the central general post office for the city.

400001.description: The general post office zone of Mumbai, located in the historic Fort area near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT).

110001.description: The central commercial district of Connaught Place in New Delhi, featuring colonial-era circular shopping avenues.

90210.description: One of the most famous ZIP codes in the world, representing the affluent city of Beverly Hills, California, known for Rodeo Drive and celebrity estates.

10001.description: Encompasses Midtown Manhattan, including the Empire State Building, Pennsylvania Station, and Madison Square Garden.

33101.description: Covers the central downtown region of Miami, Florida, acting as the main administrative financial center.

K1A 0B1.description: The dedicated postal code for Parliament Hill and the House of Commons in Canada's capital city, Ottawa.

M5V 1J2.description: Downtown Toronto harbor area, surrounding the CN Tower and Rogers Centre stadium.

2000.description: The Central Business District of Sydney, containing Circular Quay, Darling Harbour, and nearby Opera House pathways.

3000.description: The cultural heart of Melbourne, featuring its grid layout, Flinders Street Station, and arts lanes.

SW1A 1AA.description: The official postcode of Buckingham Palace, the London residence of the British monarch.

EH1 1YT.description: The historic Royal Mile sector, leading up to the ancient Edinburgh Castle perched on volcanic rock.
